players.product: AI data-center campus leases on converted Bitcoin-mining power sites (Sandersville GA 175 MW critical IT on a 20-year triple net lease, tenant undisclosed; Sealy and Brazoria TX under exclusivity)

quarterly_data.signal: CleanSpark's 10-K: fiscal 2025 total revenue (all bitcoin mining revenue) was $766,314 (in thousands), up 102% from $378,968. For its emerging HPC and AI business line the company says it is currently in the preliminary stages of building out supplier relationships, and it relies on third parties, including construction contractors and suppliers of infrastructure, for its expansion efforts.

CleanSpark's 10-K: total contracted power capacity was approximately 1,027 MW as of September 30, 2025 across Georgia, Tennessee, Mississippi and Wyoming. On October 27, 2025 it acquired rights to approximately 271 acres of land in Austin County, Texas and executed long-term power supply agreements totaling 285 megawatts for a next-generation data-center campus, with progressive buildout of power capacity over an estimated eighteen-month development period (its entry into Texas). It is evaluating existing properties for conversion or dual-use development for AI and HPC tenants and advancing design and permitting for greenfield data-center sites.
quarterly_data.figure: ~1,027 MW contracted power (September 30, 2025); 285 MW Austin County, Texas power supply agreements

quarterly_data.signal: CleanSpark's 10-K: in October 2025 it announced it is working with Submer (modular AI data center design and construction) under a non-binding framework to evaluate opportunities for a definitive agreement and the development of AI data centers in North America; under the intended partnership CleanSpark focuses on power and infrastructure while Submer delivers specialized cooling and deployment capabilities for AI infrastructure at gigawatt scale. Completing a definitive agreement is listed as a forward-looking risk factor.
